RM 101Our Story

One building, three schools, no strangers.

Alder Creek School has shared a single campus since 1974 — elementary, middle, and high school under one roof, split across three wings connected by the covered walkway everyone just calls “the bridge.” Younger students see what high school looks like every single day. Older students remember, because they walked the same hallway at five years old.

We're a public school with a project-based core: every grade level anchors its year around one long-term community project, from the third-grade creek water-quality study to the senior capstone exhibition each spring.

  • Full-day kindergarten and before/after-care on site
  • 1:14 teacher-to-student ratio, district-wide
  • Free breakfast and lunch for every student, every day
  • On-site counseling, speech, and OT services

RM 200–400Academics

Three divisions, one throughline.

Every division keeps the same backbone — literacy and number sense every morning, a hands-on project every quarter — and builds up from there.

RM 210–240

Elementary K–5

Mixed-age morning meeting, phonics-based reading, and an outdoor classroom block down by the creek three afternoons a week.

  • Full-day kindergarten
  • Daily creek & garden time
  • Specialist art, music & PE

RM 310–340

Middle School 6–8

Students choose an elective track in 6th grade — maker lab, ensemble music, or outdoor leadership — and keep it through 8th.

  • Team-taught core academics
  • 3-year elective tracks
  • Annual overnight field study

RM 410–440

High School 9–12

Seven AP courses, a dual-enrollment agreement with the community college, and a required senior capstone presented to the public.

  • Dual-enrollment credit
  • Career & technical pathways
  • Senior capstone exhibition

RM 150News & Notices

From the front office

July 22, 2026

Fall registration opens August 4

New and returning families can complete online registration starting August 4. Bring proof of residency and immunization records to the walk-in help desk if you'd rather do it in person.

July 15, 2026

Creek restoration day moved to September

Our annual student-led creek cleanup and native planting day is now scheduled for September 19, after the summer water levels drop. Volunteer sign-ups open next month.

June 30, 2026

Class of 2026 capstones now online

This year's senior capstone exhibition covered everything from wetland hydrology to a full one-act play. Recordings from the public exhibition night are posted on the district video portal.
